newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM cautious about bigger G7 role for Russia.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM cautious about bigger G7 role for Russia.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto reacted cautiously on Sunday to a U.S.-Russian agreement in Helsinki to give Russia an expanded role at the annual Group of Seven summit meetings.
"We still think that the original Seven should tackle economic issues such as development and global financial problems," Hashimoto told reporters.
But he said Japan supported Russia's participation in G7 discussion of political matters, such as terrorism and the environment.
Hashimoto said he reminded U.S. President Bill Clinton in a telephone conversation on Friday that Japan's dispute with Moscow over Russian-held islands had yet to be resolved.
The row over the islands, seized by Soviet troops in the last days of World War Two, has prevented Japan and Russia from signing a peace treaty.
In Helsinki last Friday, Clinton said he agreed with Russian President Boris Yeltsin to give Russia a larger role in the group's Denver Summit, which would be called the "Summit of the Eight."

Deputy U.S. Treasury Secrtary Lawrence Summers told reporters in Helsinki after the Clinton-Yeltsin meeting that the communique to be issued after the Denver Summit will come from the Eight including Russia but core economic issues will be discussed by the original Seven.
Leaders of the United States, Germany, Japan, France, Italy, Canada and Britain plus Russia will hold their annual summit in Denver, Colorado in June.
